newsitem.title: USA: Union, students protest U.S. oil cos' Burma ties.
newsitem.headline: Union, students protest U.S. oil cos' Burma ties.

text.p: The 90,000 member Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers International Union (OCAW) and students from the Free Burma Coalition, are holding a three day protest against oil company involvement in Burma and to call for U.S. sanctions against the ruling military regime.

"(The action) shows that there is a rapidly growing movement in this country to make oil companies and other multinational corporations accountable for their actions," said Robert Wages, president of OCAW said in a statement.
Among U.S. oil companies either with operations there or who are considering operations are Unocal Corp, Texaco Inc and Atlantic Richfield.
Unocal, which is involved in a pipeline and extraction venture said, that its involvement in Burma's economy was constructive.
"The best way to promote change in environment is not to target foreign investors who are building infrastructure in a country, without which no development will happen," said a spokesman for Unocal.
A spokesman for ARCO said the company is still at the very early stage of exploration and has not decided whether it has a commercial discovery.
